metadata.title: Master Chronology -- July 1, 1863 (Day 1)
metadata.tick_formula: Tick 1 = 5:00am July 1. Each tick = 5 minutes. Day 1 = ticks 1-225.
sources: Pfanz, Harry W. -- Gettysburg: The First Day (UNC Press, 2001)
OR Vol. 27, Parts I and II
Busey and Martin -- Regimental Strengths and Losses at Gettysburg (1994)
Hartwig, D. Scott -- To Advance or Not to Advance (NPS symposium, 1992)

events.event: Both armies on the march. Buford's Union cavalry occupies Gettysburg. Heth's Confederate division marches east on Chambersburg Pike toward Gettysburg.
Buford dispatches pickets west and north of Gettysburg along all approach roads. Gamble's brigade occupies McPherson's Ridge. Devin's brigade screens north and east.
Heth's lead brigade (Archer) passes through Cashtown and continues east. Davis's brigade in column behind Archer. Pettigrew and Brockenbrough held in reserve at Cashtown.
Heth and Hill confer. Hill insists it is only Pennsylvania militia in Gettysburg. Heth asks permission to advance -- Hill gives approval. The battle that neither army planned begins.
events.narrative: Hill's casual permission to Heth to 'advance and get those shoes' set in motion a battle neither Lee nor Meade had chosen to fight here.

events.event: Buford's pickets on Knoxlyn Ridge first spot Heth's advance. Vedette Lieutenant Marcellus Jones fires the FIRST SHOT of the Battle of Gettysburg from a borrowed carbine. Jones fires at a Confederate officer at approximately 7:30am.
events.flag: FIRST SHOT of the battle -- precise location on Knoxlyn Ridge. Monument stands here today.

events.event: Heth's skirmishers engage Buford's dismounted cavalry. Pegram's Confederate artillery deploys on Herr Ridge. First artillery fire of the battle.
events.flag: Pegram's guns first Confederate artillery to fire. Calef's Union battery (U-HAB-A2US) unlimbers on McPherson's Ridge.

events.event: Calef's battery (Battery A, 2nd US Artillery) opens fire -- FIRST UNION ARTILLERY to fire at Gettysburg. Six guns engage Pegram's battalion in counterbattery duel.
events.flag: Calef's battery must be placed precisely on McPherson's Ridge. First Union artillery engagement.

events.event: Buford sends urgent dispatch to Reynolds: Confederates advancing in force, cavalry cannot hold long. Reynolds rides ahead of I Corps to assess situation personally.
Heth deploys Archer's brigade south of Chambersburg Pike and Davis's brigade north. Both advance in line of battle toward McPherson's Ridge. Gamble's dismounted troopers fall back slowly.
Reynolds arrives at Seminary Ridge, confers with Buford in the Seminary cupola. Reynolds sends courier ordering I Corps to rush forward at the double-quick. Confirms he will hold at all costs.
events.narrative: Reynolds's decision to hold at Gettysburg rather than fall back sealed the battle's location.

events.event: Wadsworth's division (I Corps lead) arrives at Seminary Ridge at the double-quick. Reynolds personally leads the Iron Brigade (Meredith) off the road and into Herbst Woods.
Iron Brigade double-quicks through fields toward Herbst Woods. Confederates recognize the black hats -- 'That's no militia -- that's the Army of the Potomac!' Archer's brigade halts momentarily.
events.flag: Iron Brigade charge into Herbst Woods begins. Disposition changes from Line of March to Charging Line.

events.event: REYNOLDS KILLED. Shot through the head by a sharpshooter (possibly a Confederate skirmisher) at the eastern edge of Herbst Woods while directing the Iron Brigade. Falls dead from his horse. Doubleday assumes corps command.
events.flag: Reynolds KIA at precise location -- eastern edge of Herbst Woods. Tick 28. Commander succession US-001 activates.

events.event: Iron Brigade crashes into Archer's Confederate brigade in Herbst Woods. Close-range fighting. Archer's right flank overlapped. Archer himself is CAPTURED -- first Confederate general taken since Lee assumed command. Private Patrick Maloney, 2nd Wisconsin, personally captured Archer.
events.flag: Archer capture at tick 29. Commander succession CS-011 activates. 2nd Wisconsin and 7th Wisconsin sweep south of the pike.

events.event: Iron Brigade sweeps through Herbst Woods. Archer's brigade broken and fleeing west across Willoughby Run. I Corps establishes defensive line along McPherson's Ridge south of Chambersburg Pike.

North of the pike, Davis's Confederate brigade advances in three regiments. Cutler's Union brigade rushes to deploy north of Chambersburg Pike. Hall's battery (2nd Maine) unlimbers in the Railroad Cut area.
events.flag: Hall's Battery YouTube vignette subject. Place precisely.

events.event: Davis's brigade overlaps Cutler's right flank. 76th NY and 56th PA take heavy fire and are forced back. 147th NY stands alone briefly. Meredith wounded -- Robinson assumes Iron Brigade command.
Davis's brigade pursues Cutler north. 2nd Mississippi and 42nd Mississippi enter the unfinished Railroad Cut west of the pike. Hall's battery forced to withdraw under Confederate pressure.
6th Wisconsin (Dawes) detached from Iron Brigade and ordered north across the pike. Joins 14th Brooklyn and 95th NY. Dawes orders charge directly at the Railroad Cut.
events.flag: 6th Wisconsin Railroad Cut charge. Dawes leads regiment north across Chambersburg Pike then east along the cut. Precise placement and direction of charge required.

events.event: 6th Wisconsin reaches the cut. Davis's Confederates trapped -- the cut at the middle position is 15 feet deep and impossible to climb under fire. Mass surrender. Dawes demands surrender: 'Where is the colonel of this regiment?' 232 Confederates captured.
events.flag: Mass capture at Railroad Cut. Davis's brigade casualties and captures. C-2MS and C-42MS show dramatic strength reduction.

events.event: Noon lull begins. Both sides reorganize. Confederate Heth, finding the resistance much heavier than expected, halts and waits for Rodes and Early to arrive from the north. Reynolds replacement confirmed as Doubleday.
events.narrative: The 'noon lull' lasted roughly 10:30am-1:00pm. Both sides used the pause to bring up reinforcements and reorganize.

events.event: I Corps completing deployment on McPherson's Ridge and Seminary Ridge. Robinson's division (2nd Division) arrives and takes position on Oak Ridge north of the pike. Buford's cavalry screens the flanks.

Rodes's Confederate division (Second Corps) arrives on Oak Hill north of Gettysburg. Rodes sees the Union I Corps position from Oak Hill. Recognizes he can attack the I Corps right flank. Begins deploying.
events.narrative: Rodes's arrival at Oak Hill was an accidental tactical gift -- he could see the exposed Union right flank from the hill.

events.event: Confederate artillery (Jones's and Andrews's battalions) deploys on Oak Hill. Carrington's and Carter's batteries open fire on Union I Corps from an enfilading position -- devastating flanking fire.
events.flag: Oak Hill Confederate artillery -- flanking fire on Union I Corps. Must show guns on Oak Hill firing east and southeast across Oak Ridge.

events.event: XI Corps (Howard) begins arriving north of Gettysburg. Howard takes overall command as senior officer. Schurz's division deploys north of town. Barlow's division pushes to Blocher's Knoll (Barlow's Knoll) against Howard's orders.

Rodes attacks. O'Neal's brigade miscarries -- O'Neal does not lead in person, keeps one regiment back without orders. Iverson's brigade advances in PERFECT ALIGNMENT without skirmishers toward Oak Ridge stone wall.
events.flag: IVERSON'S ADVANCE -- brigade in perfect alignment approaching stone wall ambush. This is the critical animation moment for Iverson.

events.event: IVERSON'S PITS. Baxter's Union brigade (behind stone wall) fires simultaneous volley into Iverson's flank at close range. Approximately 500 Confederates shot down in minutes. Men fall in rows -- their graves visible as depressions today. Iverson reportedly does not lead the charge.
events.flag: Iverson's Pits -- mass casualties in seconds. C-5NC, C-12NC, C-20NC, C-23NC strength drops sharply. Show line of men falling.

events.event: Daniel's Confederate brigade attacks south of Iverson toward the Railroad Cut area. Ramseur's brigade waits to exploit any opening. O'Neal's repulsed regiments reorganize.

GORDON'S FLANK ATTACK. Early's division arrives on York Road northeast of town. Gordon's brigade sweeps wide around the Union XI Corps right flank, hitting Barlow's position on Barlow's Knoll from the east. Doles's brigade simultaneously attacks north of town.
events.flag: Gordon's flanking attack -- wide sweeping movement must be shown across multiple ticks approaching from York Road direction.

events.event: Barlow's Knoll overwhelmed. Barlow severely wounded -- left for dead on the knoll. Gordon personally brings him water, believing him dying. Wilkeson's Union battery destroyed on the knoll. Hays's and Avery's brigades advance south toward town.
events.flag: Wilkeson mortally wounded. Barlow falls. Gordon-Barlow encounter. XI Corps right flank collapses.

events.event: XI Corps collapses. Barlow's and Schurz's divisions broken and streaming south through Gettysburg streets. Coster's brigade sent north to cover the retreat -- trapped in the brickyard disaster.
events.flag: XI Corps retreat through town. Multiple units show Chaotic Retreat disposition.

events.event: Coster's brigade caught from three sides in brickyard north of town -- 566 casualties in minutes. 134th NY, 154th NY, 27th PA, 73rd PA nearly destroyed as organized units.

I Corps right flank (Robinson) crumbling under Oak Hill artillery and Daniel's brigade pressure. Paul's brigade commander Paul blinded -- four successive commanders wounded. 16th Maine ordered to stay as sacrifice regiment covering the retreat.
events.flag: 16th Maine sacrifice stand. Regiment holds position as all surrounding units retreat.

events.event: Seminary Ridge fighting begins. Pender's Confederate division arrives and attacks I Corps position. Perrin's South Carolina brigade drives through the Lutheran Seminary grounds. Scales's brigade devastated -- 66% casualties.
events.flag: Perrin's breakthrough at Seminary Ridge. Scales's brigade cut down. Show Chaotic Retreat for Scales's regiments.

events.event: Schimmelfennig cut off during retreat -- hides in a pigpen on Baltimore Street. Von Amsberg assumes XI Corps brigade command. I Corps remnants retreating through town.
events.flag: Schimmelfennig cut off -- note in tooltip.

events.event: Dilger's battery (Battery I, 1st Ohio) fights rearguard action THROUGH GETTYSBURG'S STREETS -- the only artillery to fight in the town itself. Engages Confederate infantry at close range on Stratton Street and Washington Street.
events.flag: UNIQUE PLACEMENT: Dilger's battery in town streets. Multiple precise positions across several ticks as battery moves through town firing.

events.event: Union forces rally on Cemetery Hill. Howard had wisely positioned a reserve (von Steinwehr's division) here from the start. Hancock arrives from Meade -- takes command and organizes the defense.
events.narrative: Hancock's energy and presence stabilized the Union position when everything seemed lost.

events.event: LEE'S DISCRETIONARY ORDER TO EWELL: 'take Cemetery Hill if practicable.' Ewell looks at the hill, considers Johnson's division not yet arrived, decides it is not practicable. Does not order the attack.
events.narrative: Ewell's decision not to attack Cemetery Hill July 1 evening is one of the most debated command decisions of the war. Jackson would likely have attacked.

events.event: Johnson's Confederate division arrives on the Hanover Road. Positions east of Gettysburg. Faces Culp's Hill. Ewell places his corps in a line stretching from Culp's Hill to north of town.
XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill. Greene's brigade on the right. Powers Hill reserve. XII Corps secures the Union right flank.
Meade replaces Doubleday with Newton to command I Corps. II Corps (Hancock) begins arriving and extending the Union line south on Cemetery Ridge. Birney's III Corps division arrives.

By nightfall the Union Army holds the fish-hook line: Cemetery Hill, Cemetery Ridge, Culp's Hill. Meade arrives in person at ~11pm. Holds council of war -- decides to stay and fight. Confederate army holds Seminary Ridge and the town.
events.narrative: The fish-hook defensive line the Union occupied at the end of July 1 was one of the strongest defensive positions of the war.
